successors.name: Kingdom of Sweden
successors.text: Western Karelia after 1293: South Karelia and the rest of the Isthmus

successors.name: Novgorod Republic
successors.text: Eastern Karelia: Ladoga Karelia, on the Novgorod side

ledger.x: 1143: first mention in the Russian chronicles.
1278: Novgorod makes war on the Karelians.
1293: Sweden founds Viborg Castle on Karelian land.
12 August 1323: the Treaty of Nöteborg, signed at Oreshek, 'the first agreement between Sweden and the Novgorod Republic regulating their border on the Karelian Isthmus'.

12 August 1323: the contest with Sweden ends with the treaty ('Novgorod ceded the three pogosts (parishes) of Savilahti (in present-day Mikkeli), Jääski and Äyräpää to Sweden'; the border 'began from south of Viborg Castle, followed the Sestra and Volchya Rivers north to Vuoksi' and then ran northwest to Särkilahti on…
1323: the Karelian lands are divided between Sweden and Novgorod; western Karelians became Catholic and later Lutheran, eastern Karelians Eastern Orthodox.

wars.name: Third Swedish Crusade
wars.outcome: A Swedish victory: Viborg Castle was established in 1293 and Kexholm conquered; the Swedish border 'is further expanded eastwards'.

certainty.note: Tribal region without a boundary on the pages; drawn as the Karelian Isthmus, Ladoga Karelia and South Karelia (the page's densest and next-densest settlement), soft throughout.
